Event cameras offer a distinct alternative to conventional frame-based cameras, delivering high temporal resolution and a broad dynamic range. Nevertheless, their raw data necessitates specific processing to be utilized effectively. This paper introduces a straightforward calibration method for event cameras that adjusts event rates and sensitivities to align with a standard frame-based camera. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach by applying it to various image sequences and evaluating its performance through existing event-based object detection benchmarks.

Graphs serve as a versatile data structure capable of modeling diverse real-world scenarios, ranging from social networks to knowledge graphs. Consequently, graph analysis has become a vital field within data science, driving significant advancements in machine learning and data mining. This survey offers a thorough overview of current research in graph analysis, encompassing both traditional methods and modern deep learning approaches. We begin by defining core graph concepts and introducing essential metrics for measuring graph similarity. Next, we examine prevalent graph analysis tasks, including clustering, centrality, link prediction, and community detection. Furthermore, we explore how deep learning techniques have been adapted for graph analysis, covering Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and their applications in node classification, link prediction, and community detection. Finally, we outline future research directions, such as the development of novel GNN architectures, the creation of new evaluation metrics, and the application of graph analysis to emerging domains like drug discovery and recommendation systems.

This paper examines the compilation complexity of the exceptional 3-qubit state $|\Psi\rangle = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(|000\rangle + |110\rangle + |111\rangle)$, which is notable for its vanishing geometric measure of entanglement. We demonstrate that this state is reachable via a 3-CNOT circuit with only two single-qubit gates, and we further establish that any circuit synthesizing it must contain at least two single-qubit operations. Additionally, we analyze the state's properties within the context of quantum compiler optimization.

This study introduces a novel technique for 3D instrument tracking during retinal surgery, utilizing a light source attached to the tool to project a bright spot onto the retina. This spot is captured by a camera mounted on an ophthalmoscope, which is then processed to determine the spot's 3D position. By integrating this data with a model of the eye, the system calculates the tool's 3D pose. We validated the approach using a custom-built experimental rig, demonstrating a tracking accuracy of 0.5 mm. Furthermore, we evaluated the method's clinical utility by assessing its robustness against variations in spot intensity, camera exposure settings, and lighting conditions.

This paper establishes a combinatorial identity for $F$-polynomials, originally defined by Fomin and Zelevinsky, by proving said identity through a determinant formula proposed by Lam, Liaw, and Yang.

This paper examines the current state of passwordless authentication, specifically focusing on the FIDO2 standard. It evaluates the advantages and disadvantages of this technology, explores its potential for future adoption, and provides recommendations for both users and developers.

We examine a Wigner-Weyl calculus adapted for lattice systems, where the Weyl symbol of a given operator is defined as the discrete Fourier transform of its local symbol. We demonstrate that this framework is capable of representing both the Schrödinger and Heisenberg formulations of lattice models. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence linking this method to the Weyl symbol calculus developed by Bialynicki-Birula and Bialynicka-Birula.

The design of online platforms significantly influences user behavior, yet the specific mechanisms linking design features to user actions remain unclear. This study examines how YouTube's interface design impacts the sense of agency among viewers. We conducted a survey of 1,000 YouTube users to assess their sense of agency and administered a task-based experiment with 100 participants to measure how design elements affect viewing duration. The findings reveal that YouTube users perceive their control over the platform as limited, and this perception is further diminished by the system's personalized recommendations. Conversely, users who actively select their own content report a stronger sense of agency and spend more time watching videos compared to those who rely on algorithmic suggestions. These results offer valuable insights for designing future online platforms.

This paper establishes that the $\pi$-calculus is behaviourally complete under both late and early barbed congruence. This achievement is made possible by introducing a novel, sound, and complete axiomatization for barbed congruence that applies to a broader class of processes known as orbit-finitely executable ones. The proposed axomatic framework is also executable, and its utility is demonstrated through a concise proof of behavioural completeness for the $\pi$-calculus.

We introduce a specific ordering for trees that ensures adjacent elements in the sequence differ by exactly one leaf. This arrangement, known as a Gray code, offers an efficient method for tree enumeration. Furthermore, this sequence is utilized to generate a specific type of Gray code for the collection of all structured trees.

The sPHENIX experiment at Brookhaven National Lab's Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) is designed to investigate the properties of the strongly interacting quark-gluon plasma. It employs a multi-layered tracking system featuring a silicon vertex detector and a drift chamber, with the upcoming addition of a new, high-granularity tracking system (HGTD) intended to enhance performance at large pseudorapidities. To further boost tracking capabilities in this region, the sPHENIX collaboration is evaluating the integration of the ATLAS Coordinated Tracking System (ACTS), a high-precision detector optimized for high-momentum particle tracking. This study details the software implementation of the HGTD and ACTS within the sPHENIX software framework and evaluates their combined impact on track reconstruction.

This paper introduces a space-time finite element framework designed to calculate jump terms for functions exhibiting discontinuities in time, utilizing an approach that employs arbitrary temporal polynomials. The method relies on a specific identity for the jumps of time-discontinuous functions, which is applied to the temporal derivative of piecewise smooth functions. This identity facilitates the calculation of jump terms for functions with arbitrary temporal interpolation. The study further examines the consistency errors associated with these jump terms and demonstrates that the derived jump-term formula remains valid for functions with arbitrary temporal interpolation.

A signed graph is defined as a graph with edges labeled positive or negative. A circular flow is a function that assigns a value to each edge, where the magnitude represents the flow and the sign indicates its direction. The function must satisfy two conditions: it must be balanced at every vertex, meaning the sum of incoming flows equals the sum of outgoing flows, and it must be uni-directed, meaning all flows around any cycle move consistently in one direction. The study focuses on the existence and count of such flows, specifically examining the relationship between the count of circular flows and the graph's spectrum. The authors demonstrate that for any uni-directed signed graph, the number of circular flows is either zero or infinite. Furthermore, they establish a necessary and sufficient condition for a graph to possess a non-zero number of circular flows. The paper also derives a formula for calculating the number of circular flows in graphs that are guaranteed to have them.

The subset sum problem is a fundamental combinatorial challenge that has been extensively researched, with numerous algorithms developed to address it. This study introduces a new deterministic approach for the modular variant of the problem. By employing the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) alongside bitset optimizations, the proposed algorithm achieves a time complexity of $O(n^2 \log n / w)$ and a space complexity of $O(n)$, where $n$ represents the count of input numbers and $w$ denotes the word size.

We present a catalog of 1,000 M-dwarf flares identified by the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) between 2014 and 2019. This collection includes 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs, with 1,000 flares from 1,000 M-dwarfs

Hemocytes are the primary immune cells in invertebrates, playing a critical role in the organism's defense against pathogens. In *Drosophila melanogaster* embryos, these cells originate from a specific region within the dorsal vessel and migrate outward to colonize the entire embryo. This study investigates the cellular dynamics of this colonization process by analyzing the movement of hemocytes in live embryos. We observed that hemocytes exhibit a unique "tango-like" migration pattern, characterized by a sequence of movements where cells advance toward a neighbor and subsequently retreat from it. This behavior is driven by the cells' tendency to maintain a specific intercellular distance. Furthermore, the cells' ability to sense and respond to this distance is mediated by the physical properties of the extracellular matrix.

This study introduces a semi-supervised speech recognition framework utilizing contrastive twin networks. By leveraging the inherent self-supervised nature of twin networks, we generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data. These pseudo-labels are then integrated into a contrastive learning setup to train the model. Our results demonstrate that this approach achieves performance comparable to fully supervised systems, even when trained with merely 1% of the available labeled data.

This study presents the framework functions for inelastic electron and muon scattering off nucleons, encompassing both unpolarized and longitudinally polarized targets. The analysis incorporates the most recent advancements in non-perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and the associated experimental data.

This paper addresses the optimal linear quadratic control problem for a system featuring a hidden Markov chain, where the controller lacks direct observation of the current state. The objective is to design a strategy that stabilizes the closed-loop system with near-certainty while minimizing the long-term average cost. The proposed approach involves constructing a dynamic controller that utilizes the history of control actions to infer the hidden state. The study establishes that the optimal solution can be derived via a dynamic programming equation, and it provides sufficient conditions for the existence of a stabilizing solution. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that the proposed control scheme achieves stabilization with probability approaching one.

Active inference serves as a unifying framework for explaining how the brain acquires, processes, and anticipates information. This study introduces a computational model of the human visual system that integrates active inference with a diverging temporal architecture. The proposed framework accounts for a wide range of visual phenomena, including the interplay between bottom-up sensory data and top-down prior expectations, as well as the mechanisms of perceptual learning. Furthermore, the model elucidates how the brain balances the competing goals of minimizing free energy and maximizing expected value.

We examine the nonlinear evolution of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) perturbations, specifically focusing on the regime where the QGP is in a superfluid state. This state is defined by a nonzero condensate of quark-antiquark pairs, which spontaneously breaks translational symmetry. This breaking generates phonon-like excitations, known as rotons, that travel at the speed of sound. These modes are described by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, which also predicts the presence of solitons. Our analysis demonstrates that the nonlinear dynamics of the QGP can be effectively modeled using the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. Consequently, we identify that the roton solitons predicted by the Gross-Pitaevskii equation correspond to the KdV solitons.

We establish that for a real Banach space $X$, the condition of $X^*$ being a Eberlein-Grothendieck space is equivalent to $X^*$ possessing a pointwise compact topology, which is also equivalent to $X^*$ admitting a weak*-compact subset with non-empty interior.

A family of maps is defined as isochronous when the convergence rate for any point's approach to its fixed value remains constant, regardless of that initial point. This paper presents a complete classification of one-dimensional smooth isochronous maps, utilizing a technique that relies on analyzing the derivative of the fixed point.

This study introduces a novel approach for analyzing the Lorenz system's periodic orbits by utilizing similarity signatures. By examining the symmetry of the Lorenz attractor, we define a similarity signature for every point within it. We demonstrate that the attractor's trajectories are confined to a surface composed of similarity signatures, a property that allows us to categorize orbits based on their specific signatures. Furthermore, we establish that the count of sign reversals in a periodic orbit's similarity signature is directly proportional to its winding number. Leveraging this relationship, we develop a systematic method for generating periodic orbits of any specified winding number.

This study examines the LAN property for probability measures associated with solutions to stochastic differential equations driven by a general Levy process. The resulting expansions are expressed as $ \mathbb{P}_\theta = \mathbb{P}_0 \left( 1 + \mathcal{H}_1(\theta) + \theta^2 \mathcal{H}_2(\theta) + o(\theta^2) \right) $, where $ \mathbb{P}_\theta $ denotes the law of the solution under parameter $ \theta $, and $ \mathcal{H}_1 $ and $ \mathcal{H}_2 $ represent the first and second-order likelihood ratios, respectively.

We demonstrate that the spectrum of a distorted Laplacian on a compact Riemann surface is determined by the geometry of the associated smooth, strictly convex domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Furthermore, we establish that the distorted Laplacian's spectral properties are linked to the spectrum of the Higgs bundle associated with the Teichmüller representation of the surface's fundamental group.

We introduce FNetAR, a new autoregressive model that integrates tokens with Fourier transforms. This approach combines the strengths of autoregressive methods, which offer efficient sequential generation, with the parallel processing capabilities inherent to Fourier transforms. Our findings demonstrate that FNetAR achieves performance comparable to the best existing autoregressive models while utilizing a significantly smaller parameter count. Additionally, we provide an unsupervised analysis of FNetAR's capabilities, showing it can successfully generate diverse, high-quality text.

This study examines the cosmological evolution of Generalized Ghost Traveler Dark Energy (GGTDE) within Saez-Ballester's (SB) gravitational theory. The SB theory extends Brans-Dicke theory by incorporating a variable coupling constant that depends on the scalar field gradient. We analyze the model's dynamics across three distinct scenarios: a flat universe, a universe with positive spatial curvature, and a universe with negative spatial curvature. Our findings indicate that the model yields an accelerating universe, a result that aligns with current observational data.

This paper examines a scenario where multiple users compete to establish optimal Service Function Chaining (SFC) paths within a Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) environment. In this setting, each user aims to minimize their own latency while accounting for the delays imposed by other users. We model this interaction as a non-cooperative game and analyze its convergence properties. Furthermore, we introduce a novel reinforcement learning approach that enables users to learn optimal strategies without requiring explicit knowledge of the network topology or the specific behaviors of other users. Numerical results demonstrate that this learned approach achieves performance nearly equivalent to the optimal game-theoretic solution.

We investigate the renormalization group dynamics of a system comprising Dirac fermions subject to random mass terms. Our analysis reveals that the random mass acts as a relevant perturbation, driving the system toward a fixed point where the fermionic propagator exhibits a non-integer dynamical exponent. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the fermionic interactions constitute a relevant perturbation at this specific fixed point.

Depression is a prevalent mental health condition that significantly impairs daily functioning. While existing research predominantly focuses on identifying and predicting depressive episodes, there is a lack of attention on the positive moments that individuals with depression experience. This study introduces a novel dataset comprising tweets from users diagnosed with depression, annotated to distinguish between negative and positive sentiments. Leveraging this data, we develop a specialized model to detect happy moments within these users' posts. Our findings reveal that, contrary to popular belief, individuals suffering from depression are not perpetually miserable; rather, they also experience happiness. This insight offers valuable perspectives for clinicians and researchers, potentially aiding in the development of more effective treatment strategies.

We investigate the isospin breaking sector of Sp(4) gauge theory with a single adjoint fermion by analyzing the spectrum of the isospin-singlet pseudoscalar and scalar mesons. Our findings indicate that the pseudoscalar mass remains constant regardless of the isospin breaking strength, whereas the scalar mass exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on this parameter. We observe a significant enhancement in the scalar decay width into fermion pairs as isospin breaking increases, which aligns with the behavior predicted by a low-energy effective theory.

We report the synthesis of a novel Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$ compound featuring zigzag magnetic chains of $S$ = 1 Ni$^{2+}$ ions. This material exhibits a Curie-Weiss behavior at high temperatures, characterized by a Curie-Weiss constant ($\theta_{CW}$) of -10.5 K and an effective magnetic moment ($\mu_{eff}$) of 2.8 $\mu_B$. The Ni$^{2+}$ ions form a zigzag chain structure with a Ni-Ni distance of 3.60 Å and an interchain distance of 5.05 Å. Magnetic susceptibility data reveal a broad maximum at 10 K, indicating a spin gap, and a sharp peak at 2.5 K, corresponding to a magnetic transition temperature ($T_N$) of 2.5 K. The magnetic structure is described by a zigzag arrangement of moments with a moment ratio of 0.5.

Smart vehicular networks (SVNs) are poised to transform transportation by enabling autonomous vehicles to communicate and collaborate, thereby enhancing safety and efficiency. However, the inherent uncertainty in vehicle data and the potential for malicious actors to compromise system integrity pose significant challenges. Consequently, establishing robust trust mechanisms is essential for the reliable operation of these networks. This paper introduces a conceptual framework designed to govern trust within uncertain environments, specifically targeting SVN applications. The proposed model integrates a trust assessment mechanism, a trust management system, and a trust enforcement protocol. Furthermore, the study examines the framework's attributes, including its operational principles, potential applications, and associated challenges.

We introduce a new nonparametric estimation method for functions that are monotone and possess a strong derivative, utilizing a monotone cubic spline approach. This method involves minimizing an objective function that combines a penalized term for the second derivative with a constraint enforcing monotonicity. We establish that the estimator achieves pointwise consistency and derive its asymptotic distribution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the method's convergence rate exceeds the standard minimax lower bound of $1/3$ applicable to general monotone functions, reaching $1/4$ for the specific case of a constant derivative. Numerical simulations confirm the method's superior performance compared to existing techniques.

This study examines a specific class of Einstein-scalar field theories featuring a potential with a single local minimum and a local maximum. We demonstrate that the resulting AdS-Taub-NUT solutions, which possess a Taub-NUT asymptotic structure, are characterized by a scalar field that vanishes at the horizon and reaches its maximum value at spatial infinity. These findings suggest that the observed scalar hair is a universal trait of this entire family of theories. Furthermore, we identify a distinct subfamily of models where the AdS-Taub-NUT solution coincides with a black loop configuration, which is defined by a closed, self-intersecting spacelike curve.

Sound ontologies are increasingly utilized to annotate audio recordings for diverse applications, including search, retrieval, and machine learning. However, the manual creation of such ontologies is a laborious endeavor, often necessitating the selection of appropriate terms from extensive taxonomies. This paper introduces a novel interface designed to streamline the manual tagging of audio clips using large-scale sound ontologies. The system employs a two-stage workflow: first, a user selects a sound category from the taxonomy, and subsequently, the interface automatically highlights image regions within the audio waveform that are likely to exemplify that category. This approach significantly reduces the cognitive load required to manually annotate audio clips.

This article presents a comprehensive overview of the dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) applied to the quantum Ising model featuring a local transverse field. The study examines the model's phase diagram, its critical exponents, and the scaling behavior of the order parameter. Additionally, it explores the model's application to the evolution of life, specifically analyzing the emergence of habitats and the development of multicellularity.

We examine the statistical characteristics of avalanche sizes within a percolation framework on a Cayley tree, specifically focusing on the branching ratio $k$. Our findings indicate that the mean magnitude of these events scales as $\langle s \rangle \sim (p_c - p)^{-1}$ for $k \geq 3$, whereas for $k=2$, the scaling follows $\langle s \rangle \sim (p_c - p)^{-2}$. Additionally, we establish that the probability distribution of avalanche sizes behaves as $P(s) \sim s^{-\tau}$, where the exponent $\tau$ is determined by $k$ according to the formula $\tau = 1 + \ln(k+1)/\ln(p_c^{-1})$.

This paper introduces a novel framework for representing the relationships between sentences within a text. By utilizing a question-answering mechanism, it captures diverse sentence connections, including sequentiality, contrast, elaboration, and causality. The approach operates in two phases: first, it constructs a query from a sentence pair to define the relationship, and second, it employs a discourse comprehension model to generate answers to these queries. These responses effectively encode the connections between sentences. We have developed a dataset comprising sentence pairs annotated with discourse relations and formulated as questions and answers to train the system. Experiments conducted on this dataset demonstrate that the framework successfully learns to represent various sentence connections. Furthermore, we have applied this method to summarize narratives by leveraging the encoded discourse relations.

This paper reviews the application of perfectly matched layers (PMLs) to hyperbolic wave transmission equations, covering both scalar and vector forms. It examines the mathematical foundations of PMLs, including their derivation, stability, and error bounds. Additionally, the discussion addresses numerical discretization methods for PMLs and their implementation within the finite element framework.

This study investigates the interaction between laser pulses and droplets, specifically examining how laser-induced heating affects droplet size and droplet array characteristics. The research focuses on the laser-droplet interaction mechanism, the resulting size reduction, and the subsequent evolution of the droplet array. Findings indicate that laser irradiation causes droplet shrinkage, with the rate of this reduction being inversely proportional to the laser's repetition rate. Additionally, the laser's intensity directly influences the array's density and uniformity.

The Internet of Things (IoT) is rapidly expanding, with billions of devices expected to be connected by 2025. This growth introduces significant challenges for IoT traffic management, particularly due to the heterogeneous nature of these devices and the resulting diverse traffic patterns. To address this, we propose a novel IoT traffic orchestration architecture that integrates Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and the Publish/Subscribe (Pub/Sub) model. This design aims to enhance network performance, scalability, and flexibility. We evaluated the proposed architecture using a simulation environment, comparing it against a traditional SDN-based approach. Results indicate that our Pub/Sub-driven orchestration method outperforms the standard SDN model in terms of throughput and latency.

We report on the detection of a gas disk surrounding the young star LkH$\alpha\,330$ (age $\sim$1 Myr), utilizing the 30-meter telescope at the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). This gas disk, with a radius of 100 astronomical units (au), is the most compact gas disk identified to date in a young stellar object. Its mass is estimated at $10^{-4}$ solar masses ($M_{\odot}$), and its kinematics reveal a Keplerian rotation profile, indicating a central mass of $0.8\,M_{\odot}$. The gas disk's inclination is $70^{\circ}$, while its position angle is $130^{\circ}$. Additionally, we detected a faint, inclined dust disk with a radius of 10 au, oriented at a position angle of $150^{\circ}$ and an inclination of $45^{\circ}$. This misalignment between the gas and dust disks suggests the presence of a massive planet. Our analysis indicates that a planet with a mass of $10\,M_{\mathrm{Jup}}$ orbiting at 10 au can account for these observations. Furthermore, we identified a distinct dust component at 100 au, which is likely a debris disk. The combined data from the misaligned inner dust disk and the outer

This paper introduces a novel concept of vector-valued distance within the space of symmetric positive definite matrices, demonstrating that it possesses desirable properties, including the ability to generate a valid gyrogroup structure. We establish a specific gyrogroup identity operation for these matrices and derive its corresponding gyroassociativity factor, which facilitates the extension of gyrotheorems to this domain.

The European Union has established a comprehensive hydrogen network to facilitate the exchange of hydrogen and its derivatives across member states. This infrastructure is essential for achieving the EU's climate objectives, specifically the target of carbon neutrality by 2050. This study examines the network's benefits by analyzing the impacts of hydrogen trade on the European electricity market, the primary consumer of hydrogen. The analysis utilizes a two-stage stochastic optimization framework to evaluate how hydrogen trade influences electricity prices and consumption patterns. The results indicate that hydrogen consumption significantly lowers electricity price volatility, while consumption in northern regions drives a shift toward renewable energy sources.

The Sun's magnetic field is highly dynamic, with its strength and orientation fluctuating across different spatial and temporal scales. Consequently, the propagation speed of magnetic disturbances varies depending on the specific location and time of observation. This study investigates how the direction of a horizontal magnetic field influences the travel time of perturbations. We demonstrate that the travel time is anisotropic, varying with the angle between the disturbance's propagation direction and the local horizontal magnetic field. Furthermore, we propose that this anisotropy can be detected by analyzing the subsurface horizontal magnetic field.

We introduce a topologically protected photonic chip designed to squeeze light, utilizing a lattice of coupled waveguides that mimics the properties of a topological insulator. This architecture enables the robust transmission of squeezed light across the chip, even in the presence of defects. Furthermore, the system allows for the generation of topological squeezing interfaces that facilitate the efficient coupling of this light into optical fibers.

This study introduces a fluid time optimal control (FTOCT) framework designed to determine time optimal trajectories for drones. By leveraging the drone's dynamics, the approach employs a variable speed metric to define a weighted Riemannian metric, enabling the solution of the problem via geodesic pathfinding. The paper details the specific metric formulation and numerical techniques for computing these geodesics, alongside an analysis of the method's theoretical properties. Furthermore, numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the algorithm's performance.

This study examines F_q-linear conjugate cyclic codes within the framework of algebraic structures over the ring R = F_{q^2}[x]/<x^n>. We establish an isomorphism between the module R and the vector space V consisting of all F_q-linear sequences of length n over F_{q^2}. Leveraging this isomorphism, we analyze the algebraic properties of these specific codes and determine their generator polynomials.

This summary outlines the recommendations of the CommF2 Thematic Group regarding career pathways and development within the field of Community Engagement Frontiers. The group identified two primary objectives: ensuring equitable access to high-quality education and training for all individuals, and fostering a vibrant, diverse, and inclusive community of researchers dedicated to advancing this field. The report details specific recommendations for achieving these goals, with a particular emphasis on enhancing the career trajectories of underrepresented groups.

This study presents an analysis of $W$ boson polarization within $t\bar{t}$ events, utilizing ATLAS detector data from 8 TeV proton-proton collisions at the LHC. The dataset comprises an integrated luminosity of 20.3 fb$^{-1}$ and focuses on final states containing a lepton, jets, and significant missing transverse momentum. The analysis targets the $t\bar{t}$ decay channel where one $W$ boson decays leptonically and the other hadronically. A novel method is introduced to measure the $W$ boson's longitudinal polarization, which is determined to be $(0.71 \pm 0.04)$. This result aligns with the Standard Model prediction of $(0.70 \pm 0.01)$, confirming the expected polarization behavior.

We re-examine the $D$-meson distribution amplitude, specifically focusing on the leading-twist and twist-3 components. By employing the QCD sum rules method, we derive the first non-perturbative parameters for these amplitudes, including the mass $m_D$, leading-twist and twist-3 moments, and the leading-twist width $\lambda_D$. Our findings indicate that the leading-twist and twist-3 moments are predominantly determined by the vacuum condensates $\langle\bar{q}q\rangle$ and $\langle\bar{q}G\sigma G\rangle$, respectively. Additionally, we analyze the correlation between the leading-twist and twist-3 distribution amplitudes and the $D$-meson decay constant $f_D$.

The power hypernetwork, denoted as $G^k$, is a bipartite graph constructed from a given graph $G$ with adjacency matrix $A$. Its vertex set comprises the vertices of $G$ and the $k$-element subsets of $G$'s vertices, where an edge exists between a vertex and a subset if the vertex is contained within that subset. This paper investigates the spectrum of the power hypernetwork, specifically its eigenvalues. We demonstrate that the spectrum of $G^k$ is determined by the spectrum of $G$ and the eigenvalues of a specific matrix derived from $A$. Furthermore, we establish that the spectrum of $G^k$ is real if and only if the spectrum of $G$ is real. Additionally, we define the signed subgraph of $G$ as a graph with the same vertex set but potentially different edge signs, and we introduce the signed power hypernetwork, which is the bipartite graph formed by assigning signs to the edges of $G^k$ based on the signs of the edges in $G$. We prove that the spectrum of this signed power hypernetwork is also real if and only if the spectrum of $G$ is real.

This study examines the performance boundaries of localizing ground stations within the Starlink satellite constellation, where stations determine their positions by measuring the time of arrival (TOA) of signals from satellites. We model the TOA measurements as random variables and analyze the resulting covariance matrix of the estimated locations. Our findings indicate that the covariance matrix is not solely determined by the number of satellites observed; rather, their spatial distribution plays a critical role. We derive a lower bound for the trace of this matrix, demonstrating that it is a function of both the count of visible satellites and their relative positions. Furthermore, we validate this lower bound through simulations and assess its practical significance by comparing it against the upper bound achievable with optimal TOA measurements.

Tidal interactions between a planet and its host star can alter the planet's eccentricity and semi-major axis, with the magnitude of these changes contingent on the planet's mass, radius, and orbital parameters. We present new transit timing observations of XO-3b, a massive hot Jupiter with a notably eccentric orbit ($e=0.45$), which reveal a transit timing variation (TTV) of $10.5 \pm 1.5$ days. This variation is consistent with tidal evolution models that predict a decay in eccentricity and a contraction in semi-major axis. Specifically, our data indicate that the eccentricity has decreased by $0.011 \pm 0.001$ over the past 1.5 billion years, while the semi-major axis has shrunk by $0.003 \pm 0.001$ AU. These findings support the hypothesis that tidal forces have significantly shaped the orbital dynamics of eccentric hot Jupiters.

The anticipated detection of the 21-cm global signal from neutral hydrogen holds significant promise for cosmology and astrophysics. However, extracting this faint signal from the sky necessitates precise calibration of the instrumental response, which is often obscured by unknown systematics. This study introduces a Bayesian signal wave calibration method designed to address these challenges. By employing a Bayesian framework, we can integrate prior knowledge regarding the signal and calibration parameters, thereby enhancing the robustness of the analysis. We demonstrate the method's efficacy using simulated data from the EDGES experiment, showing that it successfully recovers the signal amplitude with a 10% improvement in precision compared to standard techniques. Furthermore, we illustrate the method's capacity to handle calibration parameters that vary over time.

This paper examines the Gromov-Witten theory of collections of projective varieties. We demonstrate that the corresponding Gromov-Witten potential is a solution to a system of differential equations, with a proof relying on stable maps possessing marked points. Furthermore, we derive an explicit formula for the degree of these equations.

This study introduces a novel, highly consistent formulation of prime number theorems. By utilizing a weighted average of Mertens function values at specific points, it establishes an enhanced estimate for $\Pi(x)$ that surpasses the accuracy of the standard Li formula. Additionally, it refines the error term associated with this advanced approximation.

This study introduces a novel natural cubic spline approach for analyzing Alzheimer's disease clinical trials. The method offers greater flexibility than traditional linear or log-linear models, which are frequently employed in this field. We establish the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator and demonstrate its robustness through simulation studies. The method's efficacy is validated using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study (ADAS), a pivotal trial in the domain.

The escalating demand for parking spaces has prompted the development of various solutions, including smart parking systems. These systems utilize sensors to monitor parking lot occupancy and transmit this data to drivers via mobile applications, enabling them to locate available spots and navigate directly to them. This paper introduces a novel algorithm designed to enhance the efficiency of tire-mounted sensors within smart parking infrastructure. By leveraging a crowdsourcing approach, this algorithm aggregates data from multiple tires within a single vehicle to estimate the car's position and orientation. Consequently, it significantly reduces the need for individual tire localization sensors, resulting in cost savings and improved system scalability.

Level Minima Optimization (LMO) is a recent technique that has demonstrated strong performance in various computer vision tasks. This study investigates the underlying mechanisms of LMO, specifically addressing the conditions under which it succeeds or fails. We demonstrate that LMO is mathematically equivalent to a specific form of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and provide a theoretical analysis of its convergence. Our findings indicate that LMO is particularly effective when the loss landscape is highly smooth and exhibits low curvature. Furthermore, we show that LMO can be interpreted as a form of SGD utilizing a novel adaptive learning rate.

This paper introduces a novel class of reflective parametric frequency selective attenuators (FPFSA) that utilize a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) to achieve tunable attenuation. These devices operate by reflecting signals at specific frequencies while maintaining sub-dB insertion loss for passband signals. The authors present experimental results demonstrating attenuation levels of 20 dB at a 1 GHz center frequency, with a 100 MHz bandwidth and a 3 dB bandwidth of 50 MHz. Furthermore, the attenuators exhibit a power handling threshold of approximately 1 μW, confirming their viability for low-power applications.

This study introduces a novel SEIRS model designed to analyze the COVID-19 epidemic, specifically addressing the extreme scenario where recovered individuals possess no lasting immunity. The proposed framework is a variation of the standard SEIRS structure, differing primarily in the inclusion of a dual recovery rate for the infected compartment. The first rate accounts for recovery with immunity, while the second represents recovery without immunity. The research demonstrates that this specific compartmental model is mathematically equivalent to the conventional SEIRS formulation. Furthermore, the paper derives the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) and establishes the conditions under which the disease-free equilibrium is locally asymptotically stable.

This study investigates the optimal context window size for word embeddings, utilizing the Wikipedia corpus to train Word2Vec models across window sizes of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. We evaluate these models using two distinct methodologies: (1) assessing the quality of generated word analogies and (2) measuring the accuracy of word identification within images. Our findings indicate that a window size of 2 consistently delivers the superior performance across all tested scenarios.

This paper examines the maximum clique size, denoted as $k$, in a random geometric graph with vertices distributed uniformly within a unit square. We demonstrate that for a graph with edge probability $p$ where $p = \frac{\log n + \omega_n}{n}$ and $\omega_n$ is a diverging sequence, the maximum clique size is exactly 2 with a probability approaching 1 as $n$ grows large. This finding aligns with the established threshold for the emergence of a giant component. Furthermore, we establish that the maximum clique size is bounded above by $\frac{2}{\pi} \log n + O(1)$ with high probability.

This approach is capable of handling both barotropic and baroclinal scenarios, as well as stars with either constant or variable mass density. The formulation is derived from a Lagrangian action principle, where the Lagrangian is defined as the integral of kinetic energy minus potential energy. The potential energy incorporates contributions from self-gravity, the gravitational pull of a distant point mass, and rotational effects. The Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) metric serves as a spherically symmetric solution to Einstein's field equations, representing an inhomogeneous and anisotropic universe. This study extends the LTB metric within the framework of Palatini $f(R)$ gravity to investigate its cosmological implications. We derive the corresponding field equations for this extended metric and analyze the resulting cosmological evolution. Furthermore, we examine the specific case of a homogeneous and isotropic universe described by the Friedmann–Robertson–Walker (FRW) metric, deriving the relevant field equations for Palatini $f(R)$ gravity. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for cosmological evolution.

Quantum nonlocality serves as a fundamental concept in quantum information theory, yet its fragility under environmental noise remains a significant challenge. This study demonstrates that quantum nonlocality in multipartite systems can be robust against such disturbances. We establish that quantum correlations can be recovered within an arbitrary finite timeframe, regardless of the intensity of the noise. Furthermore, we prove that these correlations can persist indefinitely, surviving even under strong noisy conditions.

This study introduces a novel approach to continuously forecast web users' visual attention by leveraging historical data. The method utilizes a window-based strategy to model the temporal dependencies of visual attention, employing a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to cluster gaze data points within each window. Subsequently, attention to these clusters is estimated using a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. The model's efficacy is validated through experiments on a dataset comprising 1,000 participants performing various tasks on a website. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces a novel transmission reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) designed to actively modulate transmitted signals, offering a promising avenue for realizing intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) with active capabilities. The work details the design and prototyping of a 2x2 TRIS, followed by experimental validation using a 2x2 single-input single-output (SISO) link. The results confirm that the proposed TRIS can effectively modulate and amplify signals, with its performance closely mirroring that of a reference analog beamforming system.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves deriving an optimal policy from a static dataset, a scenario where the agent cannot interact with the environment. While recent research has largely focused on linear function approximation, our work extends the linear function approximation framework to handle general nonlinear functions. We demonstrate that this extension enables the derivation of sample complexity bounds applicable to a wide range of offline RL problems, including those involving linear function approximation, deterministic environments, and linear models. Furthermore, we establish that this approach yields a minimax-optimal sample complexity for offline RL under linear function approximation, effectively unifying and advancing previous findings.
We demonstrate that the homotopy category of a model category is equivalent to the underlying category equipped with the trivial model structure.

We report the detection of a turbulent supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the galaxy J0437+2456, identified through the analysis of its broad emission lines. The broad H$\alpha$ line exhibits a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 10,000 km s$^{-1}$, while the H$\beta$ line shows a significantly larger FWHM of 20,000 km s$^{-1}$. This discrepancy suggests that the H$\alpha$ emission originates from a region closer to the black hole than the H$\beta$ emission. By applying the virial theorem to the H$\alpha$ line, we estimate a black hole mass of $M_{\rm BH} = 1.0 \pm 0.2 \times 10^8 M_\odot$. The broad H$\beta$ line displays a flat-topped profile, indicating a highly turbulent gas distribution. Furthermore, the H$\beta$ line's full width at half maximum (FWHM) is approximately 1.4 times larger than its line-of-sight velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{\rm BH}$), a ratio consistent with a turbulent gas distribution. Consequently, the H$\beta$ line is a more reliable indicator of the black hole's mass than the H$\alpha$ line.

This study examines planar three-body systems where one mass is located at the center of mass, analyzing the associated linear relative configurations. We demonstrate that the linear relative equilibrium condition is met exclusively when the outer masses are equal. Furthermore, the paper investigates linear relative periodic orbits, finding that the linear relative straight-line configuration occurs only if these outer masses are also equal.

Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful technique for investigating biological systems, offering high-resolution insights into cellular structures and functions. However, the diffraction limit of light restricts the spatial resolution of FLIM images, necessitating deconvolution methods to enhance clarity. This study introduces a novel approach to FLIM deconvolution that integrates a deep neural network with a non-negative least squares algorithm. The network is trained on simulated data to learn the inverse relationship between blurred and sharp fluorescence lifetime images. Subsequently, the network processes experimental data to generate an initial estimate of the high-resolution image, which then serves as input for the non-negative least squares algorithm. This iterative refinement yields the final, deblurred fluorescence lifetime image. Experimental results demonstrate that this hybrid method outperforms traditional non-negative least squares approaches in recovering high-resolution details from low-resolution FLIM data.

Product search serves as a vital component of e-commerce, enabling users to locate items that meet their specific needs. While traditional search relies on textual queries, product recommendation systems utilize user behavior to suggest items. However, these recommendations often lack the flexibility to accommodate dynamic user preferences. To address this, we introduce a new product search framework that integrates both textual queries and user behavior. This approach models user behavior as a graph, where nodes represent individual actions and edges signify the relationship between them. We then employ a graph convolutional network to derive user behavior embeddings, which are combined with product query embeddings to generate a unified representation for product search. Experimental results indicate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in both accuracy and recall.

Graph embedding techniques have garnered significant attention in recent years, particularly for their utility in recommendation systems. While current methods often rely on supervised approaches that demand extensive labeled data, this paper introduces an unsupervised deep manifold labeled graph embedding (UDMLE) model designed to overcome these limitations. UDLMLE simultaneously learns a low-dimensional representation and a manifold structure from raw data without requiring labeled information. The model utilizes a deep autoencoder to generate feature representations and employs a graph convolutional network to extract manifold features. Furthermore, a graph regularization term is incorporated to ensure the learned graph remains consistent with the original data graph. Experimental results demonstrate that UDLMLE outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in recommendation tasks.

This paper introduces a new method for designing non-orthogonal sequences tailored for grant-free massive connectivity scenarios. The proposed approach utilizes a two-stage genetic algorithm to optimize sequence auto-correlation and cross-correlation properties. The first stage focuses on minimizing the auto-correlation function (ACF) to ensure precise delay estimation, while the second stage aims to reduce the magnitude of the maximum correlation coefficient (MCC) to enhance interference mitigation. The study demonstrates that the generated sequences exhibit superior auto-correlation performance compared to existing methods, resulting in improved delay estimation accuracy. Additionally, the proposed sequences achieve lower cross-correlation values, leading to better interference mitigation capabilities.

This study introduces a new framework for blind coded sensing that relies on combinatorial coding. Unlike traditional methods, this approach does not require the transmitter to know the target's sparsity level or the target's support. We demonstrate that the proposed blind sensing scheme achieves superior performance compared to conventional coded sensing. Furthermore, we establish that the proposed method is more efficient regarding the number of measurements than standard approaches. Finally, we validate the efficacy of our blind coded sensing technique through numerical simulations.

Domain adaptation seeks to enhance model performance on target domains by leveraging knowledge from source domains. While recent studies have utilized adversarial training to simulate target-like source domains, they often overlook the inherent stochasticity of the target domain. This paper introduces a novel framework that integrates both adversarial and stochastic transformations to bridge the gap between source and target domains. Specifically, we employ a stochastic transformation to capture the variability within the target domain and an adversarial approach to align the transformed source data with the target distribution. Furthermore, we propose a new metric to quantify the discrepancy between these distributions. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results in both unsupervised and semi-supervised domain adaptation scenarios.

This study establishes that all 2-local derivations on the Jordan algebra of $n\times n$ matrices defined over a common commutative involutive ring $R$ are necessarily actual derivations. Furthermore, these results extend to cover 2-2-local and local centralizers on the Jordan algebra $M_n(S)$, where $S$ represents a commutative involutive ring, as well as on the algebra $M_n(R)$.

This study investigates the gravitational lensing of a Dirac singularity within the context of Berry's phase. We demonstrate that the phase's singularity can be modeled as a point mass possessing a negative mass value. Furthermore, we calculate the lensing characteristics of this Dirac singularity, including the deflection angle, image positions, and magnifications. We also examine the lensing behavior of a Dirac singularity within the Schwarzschild-de Sitter spacetime. Finally, we analyze the impact of the Dirac singularity's Berry's phase on the lensing of light.

This study investigates the existence of compactons within a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) system, where intercomponent interactions are governed by the generalized Skyrme potential. We demonstrate that compactons emerge specifically when the interaction strength between the two components is negative. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of the spin-orbit density on the characteristics of these compactons.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, identified as the $1/2^-$ state, is recognized as the heavy quark spin symmetry (HQSS) partner of the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$, which has a $3/2^-$ assignment. This work investigates the decay of the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ into a $1/2^-$ state paired with a $1^-$ meson, specifically the $D^*$ and $D_1$ channels. Our findings indicate that the decay into the $D_1$ channel is significantly more probable than the decay into the $D^*$ channel. This result aligns with the observation that the $D_1$ meson is broader than the $D^*$ meson. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the decay of the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ into a $1/2^-$ state and a $1^-$ meson is also possible, with the $D_1$ channel again being more favorable than the $D^*$ channel. This result is consistent with the fact that the $D_1$ meson is broader than the $D^*$ meson. Additionally, we show that the decay of the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$ into a $1/2^-$ state and a $1^-$ meson is also possible, with the $D_1

This work examines the uniform approximation of $G$-invariant continuous functions defined on orbit spaces, $G\backslash X$, where $G$ is a compact group acting on a compact Hausdorff space $G$-space $X$. We establish that the algebra of $G$-invariant continuous functions is uniformly dense within the space of all continuous functions on the orbit space. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algebra of $G$-invariant continuous functions on $X$ is uniformly dense in the space of continuous functions on $X$ itself. These findings rely on the assumption that the group action is closed, a condition that is equivalent to the orbit space being Hausdorff.

This article outlines the potential for detecting Axion-Like Particles (ALPs) at future high-energy muon colliders. It begins by reviewing the theoretical framework of ALPs, followed by an examination of their production and decay mechanisms at these facilities. The authors then present sensitivity projections for various ALP parameter spaces, highlighting the unique advantages muon colliders possess over other future facilities. Finally, the study discusses the significant potential for discovering new physics through the study of ALPs at muon colliders.

Cross-layer optimization is a technique that leverages data from various layers of a computer system to enhance performance. While this approach has been extensively researched, its practical application remains limited due to the difficulty in deploying and assessing these optimizations in real-world scenarios. To address this, we introduce MetaSys, an open-source, user-friendly system designed to facilitate the implementation and evaluation of cross-layer optimizations. MetaSys enables users to easily deploy optimizations by providing a centralized, metadata-driven repository that stores system information, such as hardware details and runtime performance metrics. This system allows users to define custom metadata schemas and retrieve relevant data for specific optimization tasks. Furthermore, MetaSys supports the evaluation of optimizations by offering a suite of tools for measuring performance and analyzing results. We demonstrate the system's utility by implementing and evaluating several cross-layer optimizations, including cache-oblivious algorithms, prefetching, and speculative execution. Finally, we present a comprehensive user guide to assist researchers in utilizing MetaSys for their own work.

This study introduces a novel approach to transfer learning that combines Siamese networks with synthetic data. The method involves training a Siamese network using artificial data to learn the underlying feature space, followed by fine-tuning the model with a limited set of real data. The research evaluates this strategy across three distinct scenarios: (1) a source domain with abundant data and a target domain with scarce data; (2) a source domain with scarce data and a target domain with abundant data; and (3) two separate target domains, both characterized by scarce data. The results indicate that this method is highly effective for all three scenarios, with the most significant performance gains observed in the third scenario.

This study examines a system of elliptic partial differential equations featuring a linear principal component, a mixed-order derivative component, and a specific growth condition on the nonlinearity. The system is defined on the space $R^N$ and involves two distinct components, $u$ and $v$. The nonlinearity for $u$ is characterized by a quadratic term in $v$ and a power term in $u$, while the nonlinearity for $v$ is dominated by a power term in $u$ and a quadratic term in $v$. The analysis establishes the existence of a unique positive solution under the condition that the power term in $u$ is less than one, and a unique positive solution exists for $u$ when the power term in $u$ is greater than one, provided the power term in $v$ is less than one. The study further demonstrates that a unique positive solution exists for $u$ when the power term in $u$ is greater than one, provided the power term in $v$ is less than one. Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are widely utilized for modeling sequential data, yet they often struggle with learning long-term dependencies. This limitation stems from the vanishing gradient problem inherent in standard RNNs, which causes gradients to diminish exponentially as they propagate backward through time. To address this, we introduce the Fourier Recurrent Unit (FRU), a novel architecture designed to overcome vanishing gradients and facilitate the learning of long-range connections. The FRU employs Fourier series to represent hidden states, enabling the modeling of periodic patterns. By leveraging the orthogonal properties of Fourier bases, the model can capture long-term dependencies through the summation of multiple basis functions. Furthermore, the model incorporates Fourier transforms to enhance the learning of temporal dynamics. Empirical results demonstrate that FRU outperforms existing approaches in learning long-term connections, with applications in sequence classification and language modeling.

This study addresses the challenge of locating an optimal policy within a Markov Decision Process (MDP) defined by a known transition function and an unknown reward function. We introduce a novel algorithm, NUCB, which leverages the non-concave nature of the optimal value function to achieve a sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(H^2S^3A^2\epsilon^{-2})$. This complexity represents a significant improvement over prior approaches, which required $\tilde{O}(H^3S^3A^2\epsilon^{-2})$ samples. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical lower bound of $\Omega(H^2S^2A^2\epsilon^{-2})$ for the sample complexity of any algorithm capable of outputting an $\epsilon$-optimal policy.

We introduce a novel method for generating ultra-short electron bunches with high polarization and brilliance. This approach utilizes dual-wake injection, where a single bunch is formed by merging two counter-rotating, helical space-charge fields created by a laser pulse within a plasma channel. The resulting electron beam maintains its polarization even after acceleration by a second plasma wakefield. This technique offers a significant advantage over traditional techniques that rely on splitting an electron beam into two orthogonal components and recombining them, as it eliminates the need for complex, high-precision alignment of multiple electron sources. Furthermore, the method is highly scalable, capable of producing electron beams with energies reaching the GeV range and currents in the hundreds of milliamps. The resulting beam features a polarization degree exceeding 99% and a normalized brightness greater than $10^{21}$ A/m$^2$/rad$^2$/0.1\%$BW. These characteristics make the proposed technique a promising avenue for developing compact, high-brilliance light sources.

The universe's evolution has been marked by a progressive increase in complexity, a trend that accelerated significantly with the emergence of life. This article explores the concept of complexity from an astrobiological perspective, examining how it has developed from the Big Bang to the present day. We will analyze the fundamental principles of complexity, specifically focusing on the roles of energy and information, and discuss how these factors influence the emergence of complex systems. Furthermore, we will review the evolutionary trajectory of complexity within our own solar system and the broader cosmos, while also addressing the potential for life to develop on exoplanets. Finally, we will address the question of whether life is a universal phenomenon and consider the implications of this perspective for humanity's future.
